langCode.description: This translation's language code (en, de, pt_BR…), used as the page's lang attribute.

extDescription.message: Weighs your search results: tag, rerank, and hide sites, with lists anyone can publish.
extDescription.description: Shown in the stores and the browser's add-ons page. At most 132 characters.

commandToggleEnabled.description: Keyboard shortcut, listed in the browser's shortcut settings.

commandToggleHidden.message: Show hidden results, or hide them again
commandToggleHidden.description: Keyboard shortcut, listed in the browser's shortcut settings.

levelHide.description: A site's ranking. The five rankings are Hide, Lower, Normal, Raise, and Pin.

levelPin.description: A site's ranking: always at the top.

popupOff.message: Off. Search pages are left as they are.

popupOnLabel.description: Screen reader label of the on/off switch.

popupRanking.description: Screen reader label of the ranking menu next to Add a site.

popupNoSites.message: Nothing yet. Use the ⚖ button on any search result to rank its site.

popupKeptNormal.description: A site set to Normal on purpose, overriding lists.

popupListsAndTags.description: $1 is the number of lists (popupListCount), $2 the number of tags (popupTagCount).

popupRankingFor.description: Screen reader label; $1 is a site.

popupRankPin.message: Pin $1 to the top of search results

popupYourSites.description: Heading over the last few sites in your list, in the toolbar popup.

popupSeeAll.description: Opens Settings → Your sites. $1 is how many sites you've ranked.

popupShowOnly.description: Heading over the tags on this page's results; choosing one shows only its results.

popupSite.description: Screen reader label of the menu that picks how much of a site a ranking covers.

popupSiteChoice.message: Choose how much of the site this applies to

popupHintMine.message: Your choice for $1, on every search.

popupHintLists.message: $1 by $2. Choose one to decide yourself.
popupHintLists.description: $1 is a ranking in the past tense (Hidden, Raised…), $2 the lists that chose it.

popupHintNone.message: Your choice applies on every search.

popupYourTagSettings.description: Stands in for a list's name in popupHintLists when a tag you chose to hide or raise decided the ranking.

popupTagFrom.description: $1 is the lists that tag this site.

popupTagSite.description: $1 is a site, $2 a tag's name.

popupTagInvalid.message: Enter a tag name with at least one letter or number.
popupTagInvalid.description: Shown under the new-tag field when its name cannot be used.

popupTagAlreadySet.message: That tag is already on this site.
popupTagAlreadySet.description: Shown when someone tries to add a tag that is already on the current site.

tagSiteReason.message: Why this site fits the “$1” tag (optional)
tagSiteReason.description: Label for an optional explanation when someone adds a site to a tag in Settings.

popupThisPageOn.description: $1 is a search engine, e.g. Google.

popupNotSearch.message: Search on Google, DuckDuckGo, Bing, Brave, or another supported engine to see what Anubis changes.

hideAgain.description: Hides the results Show hidden brought back.

loadMoreTitle.message: Add the next page of results to this page and rank them together

loadMoreEmpty.message: $1 sent no results for page $2. It may want you to confirm you’re not a robot first.
loadMoreEmpty.description: In the summary above the results, when Load more results got a page without results. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreRepeat.message: $1 sent the same results again for page $2, so there are no more.
loadMoreRepeat.description: In the summary above the results. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreBusy.message: $1 asked Anubis to slow down before page $2. Try again in a minute.
loadMoreBusy.description: In the summary above the results, when the engine answered “too many requests”. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreRefused.description: In the summary above the results. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreSlow.message: $1 took too long to send page $2.
loadMoreSlow.description: In the summary above the results. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreFailed.description: In the summary above the results, when the request failed. $1 is the search engine, $2 the page number.

loadMoreOpen.description: Link after loadMoreEmpty and the like: opens the page Anubis tried to load in a new tab. $1 is the page number.

loadMoreOpenTitle.message: Open it in a new tab to see what $1 sent
loadMoreOpenTitle.description: Tooltip of loadMoreOpen. $1 is the search engine.

chipFromPage.description: Under a result's title when Load more results brought it in. $1 is the page number.

barHidden.description: In the line standing for a hidden result, after the site: “fandom.com hidden”.

barHiddenByYou.description: In the line standing for a hidden result, after the site.

barHiddenByTag.description: In the line standing for a hidden result, after the site. $1 is a tag's name.

barHiddenByLens.description: In the line standing for a hidden result, after the site. $1 is a list that only includes sites it names.

barHiddenByList.description: In the line standing for a hidden result, after the site. $1 is a list's name.

menuWhyHeading.description: Heading in the menu on a result, over the lists' reasons for its ranking.

menuNewTagPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the field in the menu on a result where you name a new tag.

menuNewTagLabel.description: Screen reader label of menuNewTagPlaceholder's field.

menuAddTagButton.description: Button after the new tag field in the menu on a result.

menuSavedNote.description: At the foot of the menu on a result, once you've ranked or tagged its site.

menuCloseLabel.description: Label and tooltip of the × that closes the menu on a result.

anubisSettings.description: Label of the cog button that opens settings, in the toolbar popup, the summary above the results, and the menu on each result.

reportProblem.description: Link in the toolbar popup and the settings sidebar that opens a bug report on GitHub.

reportProblemTitle.message: Open a bug report on GitHub, with Anubis’s version and your browser filled in

summaryShowAll.description: In the summary above the results, while only results with one tag are shown.

summaryFilterLabel.description: Screen reader label of the row of tags in the summary above the results.

summaryFilterOn.description: Tooltip of a tag in the summary above the results. $1 is the tag's name.

summaryFilterOff.description: Tooltip of the tag whose results are the only ones shown.

summaryPinned.description: One part of summaryActed: $1 results were pinned. The parts are joined into a list (“pinned 1, raised 2, and hid 2”).

summaryRaised.description: Like summaryPinned, for results that were raised.

summaryLowered.description: Like summaryPinned, for results that were lowered.

summaryHid.description: Like summaryPinned, for results that were hidden.

summaryActed.description: The summary above the results. $1 is the list of summaryPinned, summaryRaised… parts, $2 is summaryResults or summaryResultsPages, e.g. “Anubis raised 1 and hid 2 of 7 results.”

summaryResults_one.description: How many results the page has, for summaryActed.

summaryResultsPages_one.description: Like summaryResults, after Load more results brought in more pages. $2 is the number of pages, always 2 or more.

summaryAlsoRemoved.description: Second sentence of the summary, after summaryActed, when clean-up removed blocks from the page. $1 is the list of summaryRemoved… parts, e.g. “an AI answer and 2 video panels”.

summaryRemovedOnly.description: The summary when clean-up removed blocks but no result was ranked. $1 is as in summaryAlsoRemoved.

summaryShortActed.description: The summary on phones, where the full sentence (summaryActed) takes several lines; Details shows it. $1 is how many results were pinned, raised, lowered, or hidden, $2 is summaryResults or summaryResultsPages, e.g. “Anubis changed 4 of 9 results.”

summaryShortActedRemoved.message: Anubis changed $1 of $2 and cleaned up the page.
summaryShortActedRemoved.description: Like summaryShortActed, when clean-up also removed blocks from the page.

summaryShortRemoved.description: The summary on phones when clean-up removed blocks but no result was ranked; Details shows summaryRemovedOnly.

summaryDetails.description: Button in the summary on phones: shows the full summary, the page's tags, Load more results, and settings.

summaryFewerDetails.description: Button in the summary on phones: folds away what summaryDetails showed.

summaryUnchanged_one.message: Anubis left this result as it was.
summaryUnchanged_one.description: The summary when Anubis changed nothing on a page with one result.

summaryUnchanged_other.message: Anubis left all $1 results as they were.
summaryUnchanged_other.description: The summary when Anubis changed nothing. $1 is the number of results.

summaryUnchangedPages.message: Anubis left all $1 results from $2 pages as they were.
summaryUnchangedPages.description: Like summaryUnchanged, after Load more results brought in more pages. $2 is the number of pages.

summaryFiltered_one.description: The summary while only results with one tag are shown. $1 is the number of results on the page, $2 the tag's name, $3 how many results have it.

summaryRemovedAi_one.description: A part of summaryAlsoRemoved: blocks clean-up removed. $1 is how many.

summaryRemovedElsewhere_one.message: a row of other search engines

withShortcut.description: A button's description followed by its keyboard shortcut, e.g. Show hidden (Alt+Shift+H).

toolbarOff.description: Tooltip of the toolbar button while Anubis is turned off.

weighLabel.description: Tooltip and screen reader label of the balance button on each result, and the name of the menu it opens. $1 is the result's site, e.g. fandom.com.

weighLabelRanked.description: The same label for a site that isn't ranked Normal, whose button shows its ranking. Keep it starting with weighLabel's words. $1 is the site; $2 is chipHidden, chipLowered, chipRaised, or chipPinned in lower case, e.g. “Hide, rank, or tag fandom.com (lowered)”.

hiddenShow.description: Button on the line standing for a hidden result: shows that result.

hiddenShowSite.description: Screen reader label of hiddenShow, naming the site. Keep it starting with hiddenShow's word. $1 is the site, e.g. fandom.com.

hiddenMore_one.description: After a site's name on the one line standing for several hidden results in a row, e.g. “fandom.com and 1 more hidden by your list”.

summaryChangedHide.description: In the summary above the results, after you rank a site from the menu on a result, followed by an Undo button. $1 is the site, e.g. fandom.com.

summaryChangedAllow.description: Like summaryChangedHide, for Normal when a subscribed list ranks the site: it's then ranked Normal whatever the lists say. Normal is the ranking's name, as on the menu's button.

summaryChangedNormal.description: Like summaryChangedHide, after you press the ranking a site already had, so your list no longer ranks it and the subscribed lists decide.

summaryChangedTagOn.description: Like summaryChangedHide, after you tag a site. $1 is the site, $2 the tag's name.

summaryChangedTagOff.description: Like summaryChangedHide, after you untag a site. $1 is the site, $2 the tag's name.

summaryChangedSite.description: Like summaryChangedHide, after several changes to one site's ranking and tags.

summaryUndo.description: Button after summaryChangedHide and the like: puts the site back as it was before.

menuSuggest.message: Should a list include it? Suggest it to $1.
menuSuggest.description: In the menu on a result, once you've ranked or tagged the site yourself. $1 is one or two list names, each a link that opens a pre-filled issue on that list's issue tracker, joined like “A or B”.

menuSuggestTitle.message: Propose $1 to $2 on its issue tracker
menuSuggestTitle.description: Tooltip of a list's name in menuSuggest. $1 is a site, $2 the list's name.

menuReport.description: In the menu on a result, under the lines saying what each list does with it. $1 is those lists' names, each a link that opens a pre-filled issue on that list's issue tracker, joined like “A or B”.

menuMatchedRule.description: Shown below a list's explanation in the result menu, above the exact rule from the list. $1 is a line number.

menuReportTitle.message: Tell $1 it’s wrong about this result, on its issue tracker
menuReportTitle.description: Tooltip of a list's name in menuReport. $1 is the list's name.

offerTitle.description: Settings → Lists, after a subscribe link opened it. $1 is the list's name.

offerTrust.message: A list can hide, rank, and tag sites in your results. Only subscribe to lists you trust.

offerPermission.message: Your browser will then ask to let Anubis read from $1, the site the list is on.

welcomeTitle.description: Tab title of the page that opens when Anubis is installed.

welcomeIntro.message: It tags, reranks, and hides search results, following your own choices and the lists you subscribe to.

welcomePinWhy.message: Its toolbar button shows what Anubis did on the page, turns it on or off, and ranks the site you're on.

welcomePinChrome.message: Press the Extensions button (the puzzle piece) next to the address bar, then the pin beside Anubis.

welcomePinEdge.message: Press the Extensions button (the puzzle piece) next to the address bar, then the eye beside Anubis.

welcomePinOpera.message: Press the Extensions button (the cube) next to the address bar, then the pin beside Anubis.

welcomePinFirefox.message: Press the Extensions button (the puzzle piece) next to the address bar, then the gear beside Anubis, and choose Pin to Toolbar.

welcomePinAndroid.message: Anubis is in the browser's menu, under Extensions.

welcomePinned.description: Shown instead of the steps once the browser says the button is pinned.

welcomeSearchHow.message: Search as you usually do. To hide, rank, or tag a site, point at one of its results and press the ⚖ button.

welcomeSearchFor.message: Search for “$1” to see tags from your lists:
welcomeSearchFor.description: $1 is welcomeQuery. Followed by one link per search engine.

welcomeSearchOn.description: Tooltip of a search engine link. $1 is welcomeQuery, $2 a search engine, e.g. Google.

welcomeQuery.description: A search whose results include official documentation, forums, and Wikipedia, so the starter lists show their tags. Keep it technical.

welcomeListsIntro.message: Lists tag, raise, lower, or hide sites for you. You start with these:

welcomeListsNone.message: Lists tag, raise, lower, or hide sites for you. You aren't subscribed to any yet.

welcomeListsMore.message: Turn these off, or find more lists, in the settings.

syncIntro.message: Your list and settings on your other computers, and in your other browsers.

syncFirefox.message: Your list, settings, tag choices, and subscriptions are saved in Firefox's sync storage. Firefox copies them to your other computers when you're signed in to Firefox with Add-ons ticked in its sync settings. It syncs about every 10 minutes, or when you choose Sync Now.

syncFirefoxAndroid.message: Firefox for Android doesn't sync add-on data, so your list, settings, tag choices, and subscriptions stay on this device. To sync them, connect a WebDAV server below.

syncChrome.message: Your list, settings, tag choices, and subscriptions are saved in the browser's sync storage. The browser copies them to your other computers when you're signed in to it with extensions syncing.

syncBrowserHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

syncUsage.message: They take $1 KB of the $2 KB sync has room for.

syncTooBig.message: Your list is too big for sync, so it's saved on this device only. Your settings, tag choices, and subscriptions still sync.

webdavIntro.message: Firefox and Chrome don't natively sync with one another. To share between them, you can connect the same WebDAV storage in each. Koofr and InfiniCLOUD have free plans, and self-hosted options such as Nextcloud work as well. Anubis keeps one file there, anubis-sync.json, and combines the changes from each browser.

webdavHelp.message: Where to get an address and a password
webdavHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

webdavAddressHint.message: The service's WebDAV address, starting with https://

listPermissionDenied.message: Anubis needs permission to read $1 to update this list.
listPermissionDenied.description: $1 is the list host name, e.g. example.org.

webdavPasswordHint.message: Most services give you a separate password for apps. Use that one.

webdavEncrypt.message: Encrypt the sync file end to end (recommended)

webdavEncryptionHint.message: Use a long, unique passphrase in every browser (at least 12 characters). It is saved in this browser only, never sent to the server. If you forget it, the server copy can't be recovered.

webdavCorrectPassphraseHint.message: Use the same passphrase you set in the other browser. It is saved here only and never sent to the server.

webdavChangePassphraseHint.message: Anubis checks the current passphrase before changing the server file. Enter the new passphrase in every other browser before its next sync.

webdavChangePassphraseHelp.message: What happens when you change it
webdavChangePassphraseHelp.description: Link to the wiki page that explains it.

webdavEncryptionShort.message: Use an encryption passphrase of at least 12 characters.

webdavEncrypted.message: The sync file is encrypted end to end. Its passphrase is saved in this browser only; the server cannot read the contents. Use the same passphrase in each browser. If you forget it, the server copy can't be recovered.

webdavEncryptionPending.message: Encryption is set up here. The next successful sync will encrypt the server copy. Use the same passphrase in each browser.

webdavEncryptionMissing.message: This browser has no encryption passphrase set. Use the same passphrase as the other browser to read an encrypted file. A plain sync file can be read by the server operator.

webdavPrivacy.message: With encryption on, only encrypted data goes to this server; your passphrase is saved here and never sent. Without encryption, the server can read the sync file. Your WebDAV login is saved here and sent to this server to sign in.

webdavBadAddress.message: Enter the service's WebDAV address, starting with https://

webdavMissingLogin.message: Enter the user name and password too.

webdavDenied.message: Anubis needs your permission to send your list to $1.
webdavDenied.description: $1 is the server's host name, e.g. app.koofr.net.

webdavConnected.description: $1 is the server's host name, $2 the user name.

webdavWhen.message: Changes go to the server a few seconds after you make them. Changes from your other browsers come in when the browser starts and when you search, at most every 5 minutes.

webdavLastSync.description: $1 is a time, or a date and time.

webdavLastTried.description: $1 is a time, or a date and time.

webdavDisconnected.message: Disconnected. The file stays on the server, and your list and settings stay here.

webdavErrorAuth.message: The server didn't accept the user name or password. Many services need an app password here, not your usual one.

webdavErrorForbidden.message: The server doesn't let this account save files there.

webdavErrorFolder.message: There's no folder at that address on the server. Check the address.

webdavErrorPermission.message: Anubis no longer has permission to sync with $1. Press Sync now to allow it again.

webdavErrorNetwork.message: Couldn't reach $1. Check the address and your connection.

webdavErrorFile.message: The anubis-sync.json file there isn't one Anubis can read, so it was left alone. Use another folder.

webdavErrorNeedsPassphrase.message: This sync file is encrypted. Enter its passphrase; nothing was changed.

webdavErrorWrongPassphrase.message: That passphrase couldn't decrypt the sync file. Check it; the server file was left unchanged.

webdavErrorUnencrypted.message: This connection was encrypted before, but the server now has a plain-text sync file. It was left unchanged. Check the server file before syncing again.

webdavErrorChanged.message: The sync file changed during the passphrase change, or the server cannot protect it from concurrent edits. Nothing was overwritten. Sync again and retry.

webdavErrorUnconfirmed.message: The connection to $1 dropped while it saved the file, so Anubis can't tell which passphrase it has now. The old passphrase is still saved here. If the next sync says it's wrong, enter the new one.

webdavErrorServer.message: The server answered with an error (HTTP $1). Try again later.
webdavErrorServer.description: $1 is an HTTP status code, e.g. 500.
